steps.title: AO6 Requirement
steps.body: Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect. Good grammar ensures your writing is clear, professional and achieves its purpose.

steps.title: Watch out for
steps.body: Words between subject and verb can confuse agreement. "The box of chocolates is on the table" - the subject is 'box' (singular), not 'chocolates'.

steps.title: AO6 Tip
steps.body: Vary your sentence structures for effect. Use simple sentences for impact, complex for detail, compound for flow.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Using subject terminology accurately shows sophistication in language analysis. Know the difference between nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs at minimum.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Identify the error: "The group of students are studying hard." | Rewrite using active voice: "The window was broken by the ball." | What type of sentence is this? "When the rain stopped, the children ran outside."

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: "are" should be "is" - the subject is "group" (singular), not "students" | The ball broke the window. | Complex sentence - main clause ("the children ran outside") + subordinate clause ("when the rain stopped")

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read through your work to check for tense consistency Use a mix of simple, compound and complex sentences Active voice is usually clearer and more engaging Check subject-verb agreement when there are words between them Know your grammar terminology for language analysis Proofread for common errors like "could of" and "should of"
